headline: Advanced first reading of $6,420,000 loan for exterior renovations at Howe & Administration Buildings, approved $270,000 CPA allocation for St. Mary Apartments repairs
summary: The committee discussed a $6,420,000 loan request for exterior renovations to the Howe and Administration Buildings at 200 Trapelo Road and moved it forward on a first reading. The committee also approved a $270,000 CPA fund allocation for structural repairs at 88 Lexington Street, the St. Mary Apartments.
decisions: Approved a first reading of the $6,420,000 loan for exterior renovations to the Howe & the Administration Buildings at 200 Trapelo Road.
Approved a $270,000 CPA fund allocation for structural repairs at 88 Lexington Street, St. Mary Apartments.

plain_text:
Long Term Debt Committee 
    August 4, 2025  
    Minutes of the Meeting 
 
 
        Attendance 
 Chairperson McMenimen  Present 
Councillor Durkee    Present 
 Councillor Bradley-MacArthur Absent  
 Councillor Stanley   Absent 
Councillor Vidal   Present  
   
Chairperson McMenimen called the meeting to order.   
 
Councillor Durkee moved approval of the June 23, 2025 minutes. Motion was 
adopted on a voice vote.  
 
Chairperson McMenimen recused herself from the next item. 
Councillor Durkee took over the Chair. 
 
Councillor Vidal moved to hear from all off-committee members. Motion was 
adopted on a voice vote. 
 
 
1. The Mayor respectfully requests approval of a loan in the amount of  
 $ 6,420,000.00 for exterior renovations to the Howe & the Administration 
Buildings located at 200 Trapelo Road. 
 
The Mayor gave a brief presentation on the exterior work that will be done on 
these two buildings. Councillor Vidal questioned the very large amount of money 
that is being requested for just exterior work on only two buildings.  The Mayor 
said she needs to button up the exterior of these two buildings. Councillor Vidal 
asked if the buildings could be torn down.  The Mayor said they are historic 
buildings, tearing them down would need City and State approval. Councillor 
Bradley-MacArthur said she was also concerned with the appropriation request of 
6.4 million dollars for these two buildings.  She mentioned that the City only paid 
3.7 million for the entire parcel. Councillor Bradley-MacArthur asked if a pool is 
included in this building plan. The Mayor said that is still an unknown.  However, 
there is 60K allocated in the budget for a pool.  Off committee, Councillor Brasco 
said he is concerned with spending almost 6.5 million dollars on exterior work 
without knowing anything about the integrity of the interior of these two 
buildings. Councillor Brasco said it could make more sense to build a state-of-the-
art new facility.  The Mayor said we cannot build any new building in this area.  
Councillor Brasco asked if there was a need to approve this item tonight or could 
they wait for interior budget numbers. The Mayor said she needed a first reading 
tonight.  Councillor Vidal asked if sometime before September they could hear 
from some experts and get more information.  The Mayor said yes.
2 
 
 
 
Councillor Bradley MacArthur move approval for a first reading of the matter. 
Motion was adopted on a voice vote. 
 
 
 
2. CPC recommendation of an allocation of CPA funds for structural repairs 
at 88 Lexington Street totaling $ 270,000 at the St. Mary Apartments. 
 
The CPC Administrator Julie Toole and Father Michael Nolan appeared before 
the committee.   
 
Councillor Durkee said he had previously submitted a letter of support for this 
project.  Councillor Bradley-MacArthur asked if anybody would be relocated 
during this project. There will be no relocations of residents during this project.  
Councillor Durkee made a motion for approval.  Motion was adopted on a voice 
vote. 
 
 
Councillor Durkee made a motion for adjourn.  Motion was adopted on a voice 
vote and the meeting was adjourned at 1108pm.  
 
 
Respectfully submitted,  
Thomas J Magno - Clerk
